sections.html:
Parent flyer

Two versions of one flyer: a printed page for school pickup, and a post for parent groups online. Both follow Hook, Story, Offer. Fill in every BRACKET before you print or post.

Before you fill it in

  • Only write what is true. If your child has done the method at home, say what they can do now, in one line. If they have not started yet, cut that line. Never quote another parent unless they said it to you and said you can use it.
  • No promises about grades or speed. Say what the class covers. Let the kids show the rest.
  • Use the badge (see the instructor directory) once, near your name. Not as the headline.

sections.title: Version A: school pickup (printed, one page)
sections.html:
Version A: school pickup (printed, one page)

Eyebrow: AFTER-SCHOOL ABACUS CLASS · AGES 7 TO 11

Math your child does with their hands. Then in their head.

In Japan, about a million kids learn the abacus each year. They add big numbers in their heads by picturing the beads. Your child can learn the same way, here in TOWN, with friends from school.

He was "not a math kid" too

The man who built this method got C's in math. He had ADHD. He could not sit still. People called him "not a math kid."

Then he trained his brain the way he trained his body. Fifteen minutes a day, on the beads. Around week three, it clicked. He started to like it. His grades went up. He went on to a perfect ACT and a full-ride scholarship.

Same kid. Same ADHD. A different kind of smart.

Fidgety kids are welcome. The math lives in their fingers first.

A note from YOUR FIRST NAME

[One or two true lines. For example: "My daughter NAME started on the beads in MONTH. Now she can ONE TRUE THING." Or, if you are new: "I am a parent at SCHOOL, and I am a Certified Phenom Instructor."]

The class

  • 8 weeks, one class a week, 45 minutes
  • DAY at TIME, at PLACE
  • Small group: 8 seats
  • Your child learns to read, set, add and take away on the beads, then starts doing it in their head
  • A flash game every week (the part kids like best)
  • A written progress report after week 4 and week 8
  • The last class ends with a family flash round. Bring the grandparents.

Price: $ PER CLASS a class, or $ FULL COURSE for all 8 paid up front. Brothers and sisters: SIBLING PRICE. Try the first 4 weeks for $ TRIAL BLOCK.

The abacus: each child needs one. Get the free kit at childphenoms.com/free-abacus. You pay the shipping, and it comes with the parent Playbook.

[OPTIONAL, only if you will honour it: "If your child does not like the first class, I refund it. No questions."]

Save a seat

Text "ABACUS" to PHONE. I will send the details. First 8 to sign up get the seats.

[CERTIFIED PHENOM INSTRUCTOR badge] · YOUR FULL NAME · PHONE · EMAIL

[QR code to your sign-up link or your directory listing]

Tear-off tabs (cut between): Abacus class · ages 7 to 11 · text PHONE

Print and post

  • Print Version A on white Letter paper.
  • Ask the school office before you put a flyer up or in a backpack. Many schools have a rule.
  • For Version B, check the group's rules on ads first. Post once. Answer every comment the same day.

Sources
